preview: Nishtha Pandey shares her JPMC on-campus interview experience, detailing the Code for Good hackathon process, coding tests, video interviews, and mentorship rounds.
content:
Nishtha Pandey
B.Tech CS
INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE

On-campus Hiring
JPMC on-campus hiring for summer internship and FTE happens every year via Code for Good which is a 2-day hackathon.
Teams are supposed to collaborate to create tech solutions for nonprofit challenges. It promotes tech innovation for social good, connecting participants with mentors and nonprofit partners.
Eligibility Criteria:
❖Degrees: B.Tech./B.E./MCA
❖Streams or Specializations: Computer Science/Information Science/ Information Technology/Data Science/Artificial Intelligence/Big Data/IoT/Electronics/Electrical/Electronics and Telecommunications etc.
❖Minimum aggregate 7 CGPA [until date of registration] in engineering course
Timeline:
❖Registration Process: 9th March - 16th March
❖Online Coding Test: 18th March - 21st March
❖Video Interview: 27th March - 1st April
❖Code for Good Shortlist announcement: 9th May
❖Code for Good Event: 25th & 26th June
❖Internship Shortlist announcement: 19th August
❖Internship duration: 5th June to 28th July
❖PPO results: 11th August

Coding Round (60 minutes)
The online coding test conducted on HackerRank platform is the first step in the SEP selection process.
This is a programming test of 100 marks having 2 programming questions carrying 50 marks each.
The time allowed for this test is 60 Minutes.
Following were the questions I had in the coding round:
❖No Pair Allowed
https://practice.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/rearrange-characters4649/1?utm_source=geeksforgeeks&utm_medium=article_practice_tab&utm_campaign=article_practice_tab
❖Counting Bits:
https://www.codingninjas.com/studio/library/count-number-of-set-bits-in-an-integer
There was another part of the question that I don’t quite remember.

Video Interview (10 minutes)
The next step of the recruiting process is a video interview, powered by HireVue.
In this HireVue interview, you will be asked to record video responses to 2 interview questions.
The questions of video interview for me were the following:
❖What goal have you established for the future?
❖What are your achievements and what learning did you get from the same?
There is an option to re-record your response once for each question. If you re-record any response that will be automatically submitted as the final response for that question.
Link to practice: https://practice.hirevue.com/signup/3m4pjuhLArd6v5kvbT6BHv/

Shortlist Results:
The final list of all shortlisted students came out almost a month later from the video interview submission, 15 students were selected for the CFG.

Code for Good Hackathon(2 days):
The hackathon for my batch was conducted virtually.
During hackathon:
The event kicked off with an introduction to the company. They talked about the company overview, mission and vision, core values and culture, industry position, career development and growth opportunities, employee benefits and perks and social initiatives taken up by JPMC. It would be advisable to not skip this since there might be questions regarding the company in one-on-one with the mentors.
After that, the CFG coordinators introduced the non-profit organizations, their problem statements, and requirements to all the participants. Following these presentations, all teams were given time to discuss their order of preference for the problem statements.
A form was then made available, requiring us to indicate our preferences. The assignment of problem statements to each group was done on a first-come, first-serve basis according to the order of form submissions.
A zoom meeting with mentors was scheduled, it is quite important to be present in that meeting throughout the event.
There was a one-on-one with the mentors between the hackathon. It was approximately 15 minutes long, where all the mentors asked a question or two. They started off by trying to make me comfortable and talk in general. The question they asked me were:
1. What has my contribution been up to now? What part of the project was I working on?
2. They asked me how my experience of working in CFG is different from any other college hackathons that I had participated in ?
3. How was I finding it working with the team and technologies?
4. What are the challenges I am facing and how am I working around it?
5. What do I know about J.P. Morgan?
6. Since I am a student of Computer Engineering, why would I want to work in JPMC, even though it is not a product-based company like Google or Microsoft?
There were a few more questions but I don’t remember them very well since it has been quite a while. They ended the discussion by asking me if I had any questions for them.
I asked how the work culture is in JPMC and what made them stay with JPMC for 10+ years (as one of the mentors had mentioned it in their introduction).

Tips:
❖For DSA: Strivers SDE sheet and 450 DSA
❖If your team decides to work with a tech stack that you have never worked with, do not lose confidence, try to take up a part with someone who is comfortable with that stack and try to learn while working on it, try to contribute as much as you can.
❖If you are stuck on some bug and you’ve tried all you can, ask for help rather than spending more time on it.
❖Be confident throughout whenever you talk to your mentors.

Internship Offer:
After almost 2 months, the internship shortlist was announced, 6 OUT OF 15 received internship offers, only 2 accepted the offer since the other 4 got another offer before the JPMC results were announced.

PPOs:
Two weeks after the internship, both of us received a full time offer from JPMC.
